chunks: From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Temporary marriage (Al-Mut'ah) was mentioned to him. He was asked: Is it from the four [types of wives]? He said: Marry a thousand of them, for they are hired [women].
ai.seo_question: Can a man have more than four temporary wives at the same time according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Quranic limit of four wives applies specifically to permanent marriage (*Nikah*), whereas temporary marriage (*Mut'ah*) is classified as a hired contract (*Ijara*), thereby allowing a man to contract with as many women as he wishes. This distinction underscores the jurisprudential view that *Mut'ah* is a series of independent, short-term agreements rather than a single permanent bond, a key point of contention between Shia and Sunni schools of thought. The narration highlights the practical flexibility of *Mut'ah* in early Islamic society, where such contracts were widely accepted and regulated by specific conditions of time and dowry.
